claims.text: As-cast Al2.1CoCrFeNi has a fine lamellar microstructure of coupled FCC and B2 phases.
The FCC/B2 lamellar interfaces in the as-cast alloy are continuous.
The as-cast Al2.1CoCrFeNi alloy has low room-temperature ductility.
The as-cast alloy undergoes catastrophic interfacial cracking during room-temperature tension.
Severe plastic deformation followed by an isothermal hold will convert the lamellae into a discontinuous or reticulated B2 network within a BCC matrix.
Severe plastic deformation at 600–800°C will fragment the lamellar interfaces.
Annealing at 700–900°C will reorganize fragmented interfaces into a patterned morphology without full coarsening.
A temperature range of 600–900°C, corresponding to approximately 0.4–0.6 Tm, is the success window for the treatment.
Successful interface fragmentation requires hydrostatic pressure above 5 GPa or severe shear strain above 100%.
Oxygen content above 0.8 wt% may embrittle the treated alloy.
Short annealing holds of minutes to hours will avoid excessive grain growth.
Severe plastic deformation creates a high density of defects and interfaces that assists lamellar breakup.
During annealing, interfacial energy drives fragmented lamellae toward a lower-energy reticulated or discontinuous morphology.
A discontinuous patterned morphology will interrupt continuous interfacial crack-propagation paths.
The patterned morphology will promote uniform plasticity by activating multiple slip systems.
The patterned morphology will hinder void coalescence at phase boundaries.
In HfMoTaTiZrCr alloys, formation of a reticulated Laves phase within a BCC-containing microstructure is associated with improved ductility.
The treated Al2.1CoCrFeNi alloy will attain a room-temperature fracture strain above 10%.
The treated Al2.1CoCrFeNi alloy will retain a yield strength above 1000 MPa.
Heating above the B2 solvus will dissolve the B2 phase and cause the treatment to fail.

contradictions.description: The initial structure is described as coupled FCC/B2, while the proposed product is B2 within a BCC matrix. The hypothesis frames the change primarily as morphological reorganization but does not explicitly identify or explain the required FCC-to-BCC phase transformation.
